targetWord.definition: the likely course or outcome of a disease; a forecast

etymology.narrative: From Greek prognosis (foreknowledge), from pro- (before) + gignoskein (to know).

exampleSentences: The doctor gave a favorable prognosis for recovery.
The prognosis for the economy is uncertain.

clues.text: Sometimes described as "projection", this noun describes a particular quality.
Often used in clinical or pathological discussions
For ten points, name this noun meaning "the likely course or outcome of a disease; a forecast".

tossups.text: Sometimes described as "projection", this noun describes a particular quality. Often used in clinical or pathological discussions For ten points, name this noun meaning "the likely course or outcome of a disease; a forecast".
tossups.explanation:
PROGNOSIS (/prɒɡˈnoʊsɪs/)

Definition: the likely course or outcome of a disease; a forecast

Etymology: From Greek prognosis (foreknowledge), from pro- (before) + gignoskein (to know).

Example: "The doctor gave a favorable prognosis for recovery."

Memory tip: PRO-gnosis = knowing (gnosis) BEFORE (pro) = predicting outcome
